headline_marked: [[AirPods with cameras]] for AI and visual context rumored for 2027 launch
headline: AirPods with cameras for AI and visual context rumored for 2027 launch
summary: New AirPods could offer "visual context" to Siri, potentially paving the way for Apple's smart glasses.
details: Apple is reportedly planning to launch AirPods with integrated cameras in late 2027. These earbuds are said to feature lights indicating cloud data uploads and could provide Siri with "visual context" about the user's surroundings.
This camera functionality in AirPods is seen as a potential stepping stone towards Apple's rumored smart glasses, offering a new way for the AI assistant to interact with the real world.
The report also suggests a second-generation foldable iPhone is in the works, indicating Apple's continued commitment to the emerging product category.
Additionally, rumors point to a "20th anniversary" iPhone model with a nearly edge-to-edge display and curved glass wrapping around the sides.
The standard iPhone 18 may see a delayed launch, potentially running on an A20 series chip, while other 2027 models are expected to feature a more advanced 2nm A21 chip.
caption:
Apple's next-gen AirPods might feature cameras for AI and visual context, with a late 2027 launch rumored.

Apple is reportedly planning to launch AirPods with integrated cameras in late 2027. These earbuds are said to feature lights indicating cloud data uploads and could provide Siri with "visual context" about the user's surroundings.

This camera functionality in AirPods is seen as a potential stepping stone towards Apple's rumored smart glasses, offering a new way for the AI assistant to interact with the real world.

The report also suggests a second-generation foldable iPhone is in the works, indicating Apple's continued commitment to the emerging product category.

Additionally, rumors point to a "20th anniversary" iPhone model with a nearly edge-to-edge display and curved glass wrapping around the sides.

The standard iPhone 18 may see a delayed launch, potentially running on an A20 series chip, while other 2027 models are expected to feature a more advanced 2nm A21 chip.

headline_marked: Snap Unveils AR Glasses [[Specs]] for $2,195, Shipping This Fall
headline: Snap Unveils AR Glasses Specs for $2,195, Shipping This Fall
summary: After a decade of development, Snap's first consumer AR glasses are available for preorder. Specs boast on-device computing and contextual AI features.
details: Snap has finally launched its long-awaited consumer smart glasses, named Specs, at a steep price of $2,195. Preorders open June 16th with a $200 deposit, and shipping is expected this fall in the US, UK, and France. This price point positions Specs significantly above Meta's Ray-Bans but below the Apple Vision Pro.

The Specs feature a design that looks like a normal, albeit slightly bulkier, pair of glasses. Crucially, all computing is handled on the device itself, eliminating the need for a separate puck or tether. The glasses run on dual Snapdragon processors and offer up to four hours of battery life, with a charging case extending total usage to 20 hours.

Functionality includes gaming, with a 'EyeConnect' feature allowing shared multiplayer sessions simply by two wearers making eye contact. Users can also watch videos with a 51-degree field of view, record point-of-view footage, and access the internet, productivity apps, and email.

A standout feature is the contextual AI, enabling users to ask questions about objects they are looking at, providing information in real-time. The glasses come in two sizes, 47mm (132g) and 52mm (136g), making them heavier than Meta's Ray-Bans but much lighter than the Apple Vision Pro.

Privacy is addressed with a built-in LED light that indicates when the device is recording, similar to Meta's approach. Snap states users will have control over their data storage, syncing, and deletion.

While earlier prototypes were noted for being heavy and prone to overheating, Snap appears to have slimmed down the hardware for improved efficiency and comfort. The company is targeting tech enthusiasts, developers, and studios, acknowledging the high cost may limit the audience.

Specs enters a competitive market with Meta's Ray-Ban series and Google's AI-powered glasses. The high price highlights the ongoing challenge for the smart glasses industry in converting consumer curiosity into consistent profits, a hurdle Snap itself has faced with its financial performance and user engagement.
